```{webr}
# Lab machinery: the estimator of the course, the specification menu, its
# validation, and the helpers of Tasks 4 and 5 – try_spec(), my_experiments(),
# submit_exploration(), prereg(), run_spec() and report_result(). The same
# code as R/spec_tools.R of the downloadable workspace, apart from the tag of
# the class chart, which lasts for the browser session here, and the download
# of Task 3, which a browser cannot make. Every specification is fitted live
# (about a second in the browser); data/spec_curve.csv places it among the
# 192, and data/menu_options.csv gives the reason for every option that is
# not on the curve. Both arrive with the page through its `resources:` list.

# ============================================================================
# CONFIGURATION – the class chart and the course site
# ============================================================================
# The results Form that submit_exploration() and report_result() pre-fill: its
# ID and the entry codes of its seven fields. They belong to the Form that the
# cases of the course share, set up for the EU-frames case; a Form of its own
# replaces them here and nowhere else. The word in .case_word follows the tag
# in every label, so that the chart of this case reads only its own rows.
.form_id <- "1FAIpQLSezoAEOnZUfP4pkfN28_XtEBwSyc2RLsXB-h8RPSegF7_t76A"
.form_entry <- c(spec = "entry.832496914", b = "entry.1656311800", se = "entry.1337458262",
                 t = "entry.1940779437", df = "entry.1682711955", n = "entry.1586392724",
                 r = "entry.1660273001")
.case_word <- "trust"
.course_url <- "https://codemoreh.github.io/applied-replication"
# ============================================================================


# ---- The estimator -------------------------------------------------------------
# A verbatim copy of R/trust/_tools.R in the course repository, everything
# below its banner, which builds the curve; the downloadable workspace carries
# the same copy in R/spec_tools.R.

# The fits use base R, dplyr and purrr only, on purpose: the same code runs in the
# downloadable workspace and in webR on the browser lab. Fixed effects are
# absorbed by subtracting group means, so a fit on 110,000 respondents needs no
# dummy matrix. R/trust/check_parity.R checks the results against fixest and
# sandwich.

# The menu of the curve, in menu order: every combination is one specification
# (4 x 4 x 3 x 2 x 2 = 192). Anything else is refused by check_spec() unless it
# is one of the off-curve options listed in OFF_CURVE.
SPEC_AXES <- list(
  outcome  = c("parliament", "politicians", "legal", "index"),
  controls = c("none", "demog", "outlook", "paper"),
  weights  = c("none", "design", "population"),
  items    = c("complete", "available"),
  fe       = c("country_round", "country_and_round")
)

# Settings that the curve holds fixed, with the alternatives that fit_spec()
# can also fit for the displays beside the curve. Where a list starts with the
# setting of the curve, that first option is it; `controls`, `weights` and `fe`
# list only the alternatives to the options of the curve.
OFF_CURVE <- list(
  controls = c("paper_no_unhappy"),
  weights = c("post", "post_population"),
  sample  = c("paper", "all_respondents"),
  concern = c("index", "economy", "culture", "place"),
  extra   = c("none", "gov_dissat"),
  cluster = c("country", "country_round"),
  fe      = c("pooled")
)

# Outcomes: distrust (0-10, the trust items reversed) in each institution, or
# the mean of the three.
OUTCOME_ITEMS <- list(
  parliament  = "distrust_parl",
  politicians = "distrust_pol",
  legal       = "distrust_legal",
  index       = c("distrust_parl", "distrust_pol", "distrust_legal")
)

CONCERN_ITEMS <- list(
  index   = c("imm_econ", "imm_culture", "imm_place"),
  economy = "imm_econ",
  culture = "imm_culture",
  place   = "imm_place"
)

# Adjustment sets, each nested in the next, and the set of the paper without
# unhappiness, which the Multi100 instruction of Task 2 required. `soc_distrust`
# is the mean of the three items of interpersonal distrust, built by the same
# rule as the scales.
CONTROL_TERMS <- list(
  none    = character(0),
  demog   = c("age", "female", "education", "hh_income_z"),
  outlook = c("age", "female", "education", "hh_income_z",
              "unhappy", "life_dissat", "meet_rarely", "soc_distrust", "left_right"),
  paper   = c("age", "female", "education", "hh_income_z",
              "unhappy", "life_dissat", "meet_rarely", "soc_distrust", "left_right",
              "econ_dissat", "income_difficulty", "health_dissat", "educ_dissat",
              "winner", "far_right_vote"),
  paper_no_unhappy = c("age", "female", "education", "hh_income_z",
                       "life_dissat", "meet_rarely", "soc_distrust", "left_right",
                       "econ_dissat", "income_difficulty", "health_dissat", "educ_dissat",
                       "winner", "far_right_vote")
)

# The specification closest to the model of the paper (Table 3, parliament)
REFERENCE <- list(outcome = "parliament", controls = "paper", weights = "none",
                  items = "complete", fe = "country_round")

check_spec <- function(outcome, controls, weights, items, fe,
                       sample = "paper", concern = "index", extra = "none", cluster = "country") {
  chosen <- list(outcome = outcome, controls = controls, weights = weights, items = items, fe = fe,
                 sample = sample, concern = concern, extra = extra, cluster = cluster)
  widened <- intersect(names(SPEC_AXES), names(OFF_CURVE))
  allowed <- c(purrr::imap(SPEC_AXES, \(options, axis) c(options, OFF_CURVE[[axis]])),
               OFF_CURVE[setdiff(names(OFF_CURVE), widened)])
  bad <- names(chosen)[!purrr::map2_lgl(chosen, allowed[names(chosen)], \(v, ok) length(v) == 1 && v %in% ok)]
  if (length(bad) > 0) {
    stop("Not on the menu: ", paste0(bad, " = '", unlist(chosen[bad]), "'", collapse = ", "),
         ". The options are listed in menu_options.csv.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# The mean of a set of 0-10 items. "complete" needs every item answered (the
# focal rule of the SCORE reproduction); "available" averages whatever items
# were answered (its additional analysis, and the Multi100 file).
scale_mean <- function(data, items, rule) {
  m <- as.matrix(data[, items, drop = FALSE])
  if (rule == "complete") return(rowMeans(m))
  out <- rowMeans(m, na.rm = TRUE)
  out[is.nan(out)] <- NA
  out
}

# The analysed rows of one specification: the sample, the outcome, the measure
# of concern, the controls and the weight, without the rows that miss any of them.
spec_frame <- function(ess, outcome = "parliament", controls = "paper", weights = "none",
                       items = "complete", sample = "paper", concern = "index", extra = "none") {
  terms <- c(CONTROL_TERMS[[controls]], if (extra != "none") extra)
  ess |>
    dplyr::filter(.env$sample == "all_respondents" | (citizen %in% 1 & minority %in% 0)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      y = scale_mean(dplyr::pick(dplyr::everything()), OUTCOME_ITEMS[[outcome]], items),
      x = scale_mean(dplyr::pick(dplyr::everything()), CONCERN_ITEMS[[concern]], items),
      soc_distrust = scale_mean(dplyr::pick(dplyr::everything()),
                                c("distrust_people", "unfair_people", "unhelpful_people"), items),
      w = switch(.env$weights, none = 1, design = dweight, population = dweight * pweight,
                 post = pspwght, post_population = pspwght * pweight),
      cr = paste0(cntry, essround)
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(cntry, essround, cr, y, x, w, dplyr::all_of(terms)) |>
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::if_all(dplyr::everything(), \(v) !is.na(v)))
}

# Weighted group means subtracted from every column of a matrix
demean <- function(m, g, w) {
  means <- rowsum(w * m, g, reorder = FALSE) / as.vector(rowsum(w, g, reorder = FALSE))
  m - means[match(g, rownames(means)), , drop = FALSE]
}

# One specification: the coefficient of concern about immigration (points of
# distrust on the 0-10 scale per point of concern; positive = more concern goes
# with more distrust, the direction of the claim), its errors clustered by
# country (CR1, t on G - 1 df, the rule of the curve), the conventional test,
# and the partial correlation by the Multi100 rule.
fit_spec <- function(ess, outcome = "parliament", controls = "paper", weights = "none",
                     items = "complete", fe = "country_round", sample = "paper",
                     concern = "index", extra = "none", cluster = "country") {
  check_spec(outcome, controls, weights, items, fe, sample, concern, extra, cluster)
  frame <- spec_frame(ess, outcome, controls, weights, items, sample, concern, extra)
  terms <- c("x", CONTROL_TERMS[[controls]], if (extra != "none") extra)
  x <- as.matrix(frame[, terms])
  w <- frame$w

  # Round dummies for every round present but the first, so that a subset of
  # rounds still fits
  if (fe == "country_and_round") {
    shifts <- sort(unique(frame$essround))[-1]
    rounds <- outer(frame$essround, shifts, `==`) * 1
    colnames(rounds) <- paste0("round", shifts)
    x <- cbind(x, rounds)
  }
  absorbed <- switch(fe, country_round = frame$cr, country_and_round = frame$cntry,
                     pooled = rep("all", nrow(frame)))
  m <- demean(cbind(y = frame$y, x), absorbed, w)
  yt <- m[, 1]
  xt <- m[, -1, drop = FALSE]

  bread <- solve(crossprod(xt, w * xt))
  beta <- drop(bread %*% crossprod(xt, w * yt))
  e <- yt - drop(xt %*% beta)
  n <- nrow(xt)
  k <- ncol(xt)
  n_fe <- length(unique(absorbed))

  # Conventional (model-based) errors, with the absorbed groups in the df
  df_conv <- n - k - n_fe
  se_conv <- sqrt(sum(w * e^2) / df_conv * bread[1, 1])

  # Cluster-robust CR1 errors. Groups absorbed inside the clusters do not count
  # in K, apart from one that stands for the intercept (the default of fixest).
  groups <- if (cluster == "country") frame$cntry else frame$cr
  n_cl <- length(unique(groups))
  scores <- rowsum(xt * (w * e), groups)
  k_ssc <- k + 1
  adj <- n_cl / (n_cl - 1) * (n - 1) / (n - k_ssc)
  se <- sqrt(adj * (bread %*% crossprod(scores) %*% bread)[1, 1])

  b <- beta[[1]]
  t_cl <- b / se
  t_conv <- b / se_conv
  data.frame(
    outcome = outcome, controls = controls, weights = weights, items = items, fe = fe,
    sample = sample, concern = concern, extra = extra, cluster = cluster,
    b = b, se = se, stat_type = "t", stat = t_cl, df = n_cl - 1,
    p = 2 * stats::pt(-abs(t_cl), n_cl - 1),
    se_conv = se_conv, t_conv = t_conv, df_conv = df_conv,
    p_conv = 2 * stats::pt(-abs(t_conv), df_conv),
    r = r_multi100(t_conv, "t", df_conv, n),
    b_std = b * stats::sd(frame$x) / stats::sd(frame$y),
    n = n, n_clusters = n_cl, n_country_rounds = length(unique(frame$cr))
  )
}

# The conversion rules of Multi100 (standard_correlation_coefficient.R): t with
# its df; z with the sample size standing in for the missing df; F with one
# numerator df read as the square of a t.
r_multi100 <- function(stat, stat_type, df, n) {
  stat_type <- rep_len(stat_type, length(stat))
  dplyr::case_when(
    stat_type == "t" ~ stat / sqrt(stat^2 + df),
    stat_type == "z" ~ tanh(abs(stat) * sqrt(1 / (n - 3))) * sign(stat),
    stat_type == "F" ~ sqrt(stat / (stat + df))
  )
}

# The free-text label that carries a specification to the class chart.
spec_line <- function(outcome, controls, weights, items, fe) {
  sprintf("outcome=%s controls=%s weights=%s items=%s fe=%s", outcome, controls, weights, items, fe)
}


# ---- The menu --------------------------------------------------------------------
# The twelve decisions in the order of the menu, each with the options that
# the curve keeps. The five decisions of SPEC_AXES keep two or more options,
# which multiply to the 192 specifications; on the other seven the curve keeps
# one. Every other option is a row of data/menu_options.csv, whose reason the
# helpers print when it is asked for.
.menu <- list(
  # Level 1 – Estimands
  outcome   = SPEC_AXES$outcome,
  controls  = SPEC_AXES$controls,
  weights   = SPEC_AXES$weights,
  sample    = "paper",
  # Level 2 – Measurement
  concern   = "index",
  items     = SPEC_AXES$items,
  education = "five",
  votes     = "cabinet",
  missing   = "listwise",
  # Level 3 – Estimation
  fe        = SPEC_AXES$fe,
  errors    = "country",
  scale     = "points"
)
.level_titles <- c(estimand    = "Level 1 – Estimands",
                   measurement = "Level 2 – Measurement",
                   estimation  = "Level 3 – Estimation")


# ---- The shipped files -----------------------------------------------------------
# Each file is read once and cached, apart from the copy of the data that the
# page loads as `ess`, so that edits made to that copy in a task never reach
# the helpers. The base reader keeps this code identical, line for line, with
# the copy in R/spec_tools.R of the workspace; it reads the empty cells of the
# extract as NA, as readr does.
.cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
.read_once <- function(name, path) {
  if (is.null(.cache[[name]])) {
    if (!file.exists(path))
      stop(sprintf("%s is missing – the page loads it through its resources list. Reload the page.",
                   path), call. = FALSE)
    assign(name, utils::read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8", # r-style: keep – the same reader as the workspace
                                 na.strings = c("", "NA")),
           envir = .cache)
  }
  .cache[[name]]
}
.ess     <- function() .read_once("ess", "data/trust_ess.csv")
.curve   <- function() .read_once("curve", "data/spec_curve.csv")
.options <- function() .read_once("options", "data/menu_options.csv")

# The extract that the setup cell has just read goes into the cache as it is,
# so that the helpers never read the 10 MB file a second time. An edit to
# `ess` in a task makes a new copy and leaves the cached one untouched.
if (exists("ess")) assign("ess", ess, envir = .cache)


# ---- Pages of the course site ----------------------------------------------------
.pages <- c(
  "cases/trust/index.qmd"       = "Case study",
  "cases/trust/menu.qmd"        = "Specification menu",
  "cases/trust/map.qmd"         = "Decision map",
  "cases/trust/multiverse.qmd"  = "Multiverse",
  "companion/dags.qmd"          = "Causal graphs and adjustment sets",
  "companion/measurement.qmd"   = "The items behind the scales",
  "companion/weighting.qmd"     = "Weights",
  "companion/missingness.qmd"   = "Missing answers",
  "companion/stats-methods.qmd" = "The statistical methods behind the course",
  "companion/multiverse.qmd"    = "The multiverse and its critics")
.page_ref <- function(path) {
  title <- if (path %in% names(.pages)) .pages[[path]] else path
  sprintf("%s, %s/%s", title, .course_url, sub("\\.qmd$", ".html", path))
}
.or_list <- function(x) {
  q <- paste0("\"", x, "\"")
  if (length(q) == 1) q else paste(paste(q[-length(q)], collapse = ", "), "or", q[length(q)])
}


# ---- Validation ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two entry points into the same rules. .validate() takes a named list, which
# is how try_spec() supplies its arguments; .check_choices() reads the twelve
# my_* choices of the preregistration cell. An option that is not on the
# curve stops with the reason from menu_options.csv, the page of the course
# site that teaches it, and the options that stay on the curve.
.on_menu <- function(axis, v) is.character(v) && length(v) == 1 && !is.na(v) && v %in% .menu[[axis]]

.refuse <- function(axis, v, as_args) {
  shown <- if (as_args) axis else paste0("my_", axis)
  keep  <- .menu[[axis]]
  map   <- paste0("  Every decision and its options: ", .page_ref("cases/trust/map.qmd"))
  if (!is.character(v) || length(v) != 1 || is.na(v))
    stop(sprintf("%s needs one option in quotes, for example %s = \"%s\".", shown, shown, keep[1]),
         call. = FALSE)
  opts <- .options()
  row  <- dplyr::filter(opts, .data$axis == .env$axis, .data$option == .env$v)
  off  <- dplyr::filter(opts, .data$axis == .env$axis, !.data$on_curve)$option
  msg <- if (nrow(row) == 1) c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" (%s) is not on the curve of %d specifications, so it has no result here.",
            shown, v, row$label, nrow(.curve())),
    paste0("  Why: ", row$reason),
    paste0("  Where it is taught: ", .page_ref(row$taught_on)),
    map,
    sprintf("  To stay on the curve, choose %s = %s.", shown, .or_list(keep))
  ) else c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" is not an option on the menu.", shown, v),
    sprintf("  On the curve: %s.", paste(keep, collapse = " | ")),
    if (length(off) > 0)
      sprintf("  Off the curve, refused with the reason why: %s.", paste(off, collapse = " | ")),
    map
  )
  stop(paste(msg, collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
}

.validate <- function(ch, as_args = FALSE) {
  bad <- purrr::discard(names(.menu), \(a) .on_menu(a, ch[[a]]))
  if (length(bad) > 0) .refuse(bad[1], ch[[bad[1]]], as_args)
  ch[names(.menu)]
}

# The choices are looked up from the frame of this function outwards, which
# reaches the session in which the preregistration cell was run.
.check_choices <- function() {
  need <- paste0("my_", names(.menu))
  ch <- mget(need, envir = environment(), inherits = TRUE, ifnotfound = list(NULL))
  missing <- need[purrr::map_lgl(ch, is.null)]
  if (length(missing) > 0)
    stop("Not declared yet: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         ". Fill in every choice in the preregistration cell and run it first.", call. = FALSE)
  .validate(stats::setNames(ch, names(.menu)))
}


# ---- The live fit ----------------------------------------------------------------
# fit_spec() on the five decisions that vary on the curve, with the 95%
# interval of the estimate (t on 15 df, from the errors clustered by country)
# and the place of the result among the 192. The fit is checked against its
# row of data/spec_curve.csv; a difference means that the page loaded an
# incomplete file.
.result <- function(ch) {
  fit <- fit_spec(.ess(), ch$outcome, ch$controls, ch$weights, ch$items, ch$fe) |>
    as.list()
  crit <- stats::qt(0.975, fit$df)
  curve <- .curve()
  stored <- dplyr::filter(curve, .data$outcome == ch$outcome, .data$controls == ch$controls,
                          .data$weights == ch$weights, .data$items == ch$items,
                          .data$fe == ch$fe)
  if (nrow(stored) != 1) {
    warning("This specification has no row in data/spec_curve.csv; reload the page.",
            call. = FALSE)
  } else if (abs(fit$b - stored$b) > 1e-6 || abs(fit$stat - stored$stat) > 1e-6) {
    warning(sprintf("The live fit (b = %.5f, t = %.3f) differs from the curve that this page loaded (b = %.5f, t = %.3f). Reload the page.",
                    fit$b, fit$stat, stored$b, stored$stat),
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  c(fit, list(ci_low = fit$b - crit * fit$se, ci_high = fit$b + crit * fit$se,
              larger = sum(curve$b > fit$b + 1e-9), n_curve = nrow(curve)))
}


# ---- The printout ----------------------------------------------------------------
.fmt_p <- function(p) if (p < 1e-4) "< 0.0001" else sprintf("= %s", format(signif(p, 2), scientific = FALSE))
.fmt_n <- function(n) format(round(n), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)

.class_line <- function(res) {
  above <- res$b > 0
  sig   <- res$p < 0.05
  if (above && sig) "above zero and significant at 5%, in the direction of the claim"
  else if (above) "above zero, but not significant at 5%"
  else if (sig) "below zero and significant at 5%, against the direction of the claim"
  else "below zero and not significant at 5%"
}

.print_result <- function(ch, res, lead = NULL) {
  writeLines(c(
    lead,
    paste0("  ", spec_line(ch$outcome, ch$controls, ch$weights, ch$items, ch$fe)),
    sprintf("  Estimate: %.4f points of distrust per point of concern, 95%% interval %.3f to %.3f",
            res$b, res$ci_low, res$ci_high),
    sprintf("  Test: t = %.2f on %d df, p %s (errors clustered by country, %d countries)",
            res$stat, round(res$df), .fmt_p(res$p), res$n_clusters),
    sprintf("        conventional errors, which treat respondents as independent: t = %.2f on %s df",
            res$t_conv, .fmt_n(res$df_conv)),
    sprintf("  n = %s respondents in %d country-rounds, partial r = %.3f (the conversion rule of Multi100)",
            .fmt_n(res$n), res$n_country_rounds, res$r),
    paste0("  Verdict: ", .class_line(res)),
    sprintf("  On the curve: %d of the %d specifications have a larger estimate",
            res$larger, res$n_curve)))
  invisible(res)
}


# ---- Task 4: the exploratory helpers -----------------------------------------------
.tried <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
assign("log", NULL, envir = .tried)
assign("last", NULL, envir = .tried)

# The first five arguments are the decisions on which the curve keeps more
# than one option; the other seven are fixed on the curve, and asking for any
# other option of theirs prints the reason why it is not on the curve.
try_spec <- function(outcome = "parliament", controls = "paper", weights = "none",
                     items = "complete", fe = "country_round", sample = "paper",
                     concern = "index", education = "five", votes = "cabinet",
                     missing = "listwise", errors = "country", scale = "points") {
  ch <- .validate(list(outcome = outcome, controls = controls, weights = weights,
                       sample = sample, concern = concern, items = items,
                       education = education, votes = votes, missing = missing,
                       fe = fe, errors = errors, scale = scale), as_args = TRUE)
  res <- .result(ch)
  .print_result(ch, res, lead = "")
  row <- data.frame(ch, b = res$b, ci_low = res$ci_low, ci_high = res$ci_high,
                    t = res$stat, p = res$p, n = res$n, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  assign("log", dplyr::bind_rows(.tried$log, row), envir = .tried)
  assign("last", list(ch = ch, res = res), envir = .tried)
  invisible(row)
}

# The running log of everything try_spec() has fitted. Only the decisions that
# varied are shown; the others are those of the reference specification.
my_experiments <- function() {
  d <- .tried$log
  if (is.null(d)) {
    writeLines("Nothing tried yet – call try_spec() at least once.")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  varied <- purrr::keep(names(.menu), \(a) dplyr::n_distinct(d[[a]]) > 1)
  show <- d |>
    dplyr::transmute(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(varied)),

            ph[["education"]], ph[["votes"]], ph[["missing"]]),
```

## Task 2, continued – The estimand and the graph {#task-2-estimand-and-graph}

Before fitting anything, say what you are trying to estimate, in words. A template that you can adapt [@LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand]:

> The **unit-specific quantity** is, for each respondent, the difference between the distrust of parliament that they would report if they were one point more concerned about immigration and the distrust that they report now. The **target population** is the citizens of the 16 Western European countries in 2002–2009 who do not belong to an ethnic minority.

There is a catch in that sentence. Nobody observes the same respondent at two levels of concern: the ESS interviewed different people in each round, so the data can only compare respondents who differ in concern. Whether that comparison answers the question depends on what else differs between them.

A causal graph sets this out. A graph of this kind is a diagram of what causes what: variables are nodes, arrows run from cause to effect, and the rules for reading the graph say which paths between concern and distrust are open, given what the comparison holds constant. The graph below is written in ordinary R, one arrow per string, each written the way it is drawn: `"pessimism -> concern"` is the arrow from a pessimistic outlook to concern about immigration. Background characteristics (age, sex, education, income), a general pessimism and ideology can each shape both concern and distrust, which makes them possible confounders. A vote for a far-right party and the verdict on public services and the economy may follow from concern, from distrust, or from both. One arrow is switched off with a `#`: the arrow from concern to distrust, which is the effect that the claim is about.


::: {.cell autorun='true'}
```{webr}
#| include: false
#| autorun: true
# Graph machinery for Task 2. dagitty runs its graph algorithms in a
# JavaScript engine that a browser grants only to a page served with
# cross-origin isolation headers (COOP and COEP); without them the call fails
# with a JavaScript error that tryCatch() cannot catch. The functions below
# answer the questions of Task 2 in R instead: make_dag() builds the graph,
# adjustmentSets() returns the minimal adjustment sets for the total effect,
# isAdjustmentSet() checks one set, paths() lists the paths between two nodes
# and whether each is open given a conditioning set Z, and plot_dag() draws
# the graph with ggplot2. They agree with dagitty on every graph of this
# task, and plot_dag() also draws a graph that dagitty built.

# Where each node sits in the figure, with y counted upwards: concern on the
# left, distrust on the right, the possible common causes above the line
# between them and the possible consequences below it. A node without a
# position here is drawn on a row below the graph.
.dag_xy <- list(concern = c(0, 0), distrust = c(4, 0), background = c(2, 2.4),
                pessimism = c(0.7, 1.5), ideology = c(3.3, 1.5),
                far_right = c(2, -1.1), services = c(2, -2.1))
dag_engine <- "built-in"

.make_dag_builtin <- function(..., exposure, outcome, latent) {
  arrows <- c(...)
  edges <- purrr::map(arrows, \(a) {
    ends <- trimws(strsplit(a, "->", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
    if (length(ends) < 2 || !all(nzchar(ends)) || grepl("<-", a, fixed = TRUE))
      stop(sprintf("Write each arrow as \"cause -> effect\", for example \"pessimism -> concern\"; \"%s\" is not one.",
                   a), call. = FALSE)
    data.frame(from = ends[-length(ends)], to = ends[-1])
  }) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows() |>
    dplyr::distinct()
  structure(list(edges = edges, nodes = unique(c(exposure, outcome, edges$from, edges$to)),
                 exposure = exposure, outcome = outcome, latent = latent),
            class = "simple_dag")
}

# The same graph as a dagitty object, as R/dag_starter.R of the workspace
# builds it; dagitty counts y downwards, so the heights change sign.
.make_dag_dagitty <- function(..., exposure, outcome, latent) {
  arrows <- c(...)
  nodes <- unique(c(exposure, outcome, trimws(unlist(strsplit(arrows, "->|<-")))))
  declare <- purrr::map_chr(nodes, \(v) {
    tags <- c(if (v %in% exposure) "exposure",
              if (v %in% outcome) "outcome",
              if (v %in% latent) "latent",
              if (v %in% names(.dag_xy))
                sprintf("pos=\"%s,%s\"", .dag_xy[[v]][1], -.dag_xy[[v]][2]))
    if (length(tags) == 0) v else sprintf("%s [%s]", v, paste(tags, collapse = ","))
  })
  dagitty::dagitty(paste0("dag {\n", paste(c(declare, arrows), collapse = "\n"), "\n}"))
}

# A graph from arrows written "cause -> effect", one per string. The named
# arguments come last, so that switching off the last arrow with a # never
# leaves a comma dangling.
make_dag <- function(..., exposure = "concern", outcome = "distrust", latent = character(0)) {
  build <- if (identical(dag_engine, "dagitty")) .make_dag_dagitty else .make_dag_builtin
  build(..., exposure = exposure, outcome = outcome, latent = latent)
}

.dag_has_edge <- function(dag, a, b) any(dag$edges$from == a & dag$edges$to == b)

# A node counts as one of its own descendants, which is what the collider rule
# below needs.
.dag_descendants <- function(dag, v) {
  kids <- setdiff(dag$edges$to[dag$edges$from %in% v], v)
  if (length(kids) == 0) v else .dag_descendants(dag, union(v, kids))
}

# Every simple path between two nodes, ignoring the direction of the arrows.
# The recursion is safe only because a teaching graph is tiny.
.dag_paths <- function(dag, from, to) {
  neighbours <- \(v) unique(c(dag$edges$to[dag$edges$from == v], dag$edges$from[dag$edges$to == v]))
  extend <- function(path) {
    v <- path[length(path)]
    if (v == to) return(list(path))
    purrr::list_flatten(purrr::map(setdiff(neighbours(v), path), \(w) extend(c(path, w))))
  }
  extend(from)
}

# A path is blocked by the set z if any node along it is either a non-collider
# inside z, or a collider with no descendant in z.
.dag_path_blocked <- function(dag, path, z) {
  if (length(path) < 3L) return(FALSE)
  purrr::some(seq(2L, length(path) - 1L), \(i) {
    node <- path[i]
    collider <- .dag_has_edge(dag, path[i - 1L], node) && .dag_has_edge(dag, path[i + 1L], node)
    if (collider) !any(.dag_descendants(dag, node) %in% z) else node %in% z
  })
}

# The backdoor criterion: a set qualifies if it holds no descendant of the
# exposure and blocks every path that starts with an arrow into the exposure.
.closes_backdoors <- function(x, z, exposure = x$exposure, outcome = x$outcome) {
  backdoor <- purrr::keep(.dag_paths(x, exposure, outcome), \(p) .dag_has_edge(x, p[2L], exposure))
  !any(z %in% .dag_descendants(x, exposure)) &&
    purrr::every(backdoor, \(p) .dag_path_blocked(x, p, z))
}

# Brute-forced over subsets of the observed variables that are not
# descendants of the exposure: smallest sets first, and a set is skipped once
# it contains a set already found, which leaves the minimal ones.
.adjustment_sets_builtin <- function(x, exposure = x$exposure, outcome = x$outcome,
                                     effect = "total", ...) {
  if (!identical(effect, "total"))
    stop("The graph code built into this page answers the total effect only; paths() shows what a conditioning set opens and closes.",
         call. = FALSE)
  candidates <- setdiff(x$nodes, c(outcome, x$latent, .dag_descendants(x, exposure)))
  subsets <- c(list(character(0)),
               purrr::list_flatten(purrr::map(seq_along(candidates),
                                              \(k) utils::combn(candidates, k, simplify = FALSE))))
  closing <- purrr::keep(subsets, \(z) .closes_backdoors(x, z, exposure, outcome))
  minimal <- purrr::reduce(closing, \(found, z)
    if (purrr::some(found, \(f) all(f %in% z))) found else c(found, list(sort(z))), .init = list())

# The paths between two nodes, each with its arrows, and whether it is open
# given the conditioning set Z; sorted as dagitty sorts them.
.paths_builtin <- function(x, from = x$exposure, to = x$outcome, Z = character(0), ...) {
  found <- .dag_paths(x, from, to)
  label <- purrr::map_chr(found, \(p) {
    steps <- purrr::map_chr(seq_len(length(p) - 1L),
                            \(i) if (.dag_has_edge(x, p[i], p[i + 1L])) " -> " else " <- ")
    paste0(p[1], paste0(steps, p[-1], collapse = ""))
  })
  open <- purrr::map_lgl(found, \(p) !.dag_path_blocked(x, p, Z))
  ord <- order(label, method = "radix")
  list(paths = label[ord], open = open[ord])
}

# The figure, for a graph from either engine. Colour marks the exposure and
# the outcome. Each arrow stops at the edge of the box of its target.
.dag_parts <- function(d) {
  if (inherits(d, "dagitty")) {
    xy <- dagitty::coordinates(d)
    list(nodes = data.frame(name = names(xy$x), x = unname(xy$x), y = -unname(xy$y)),
         edges = dplyr::transmute(dagitty::edges(d), from = as.character(.data$v),
                                  to = as.character(.data$w)),
         exposure = dagitty::exposures(d), outcome = dagitty::outcomes(d),
         latent = dagitty::latents(d))
  } else {
    at <- \(v, k) if (v %in% names(.dag_xy)) .dag_xy[[v]][k] else NA_real_
    list(nodes = data.frame(name = d$nodes, x = purrr::map_dbl(d$nodes, \(v) at(v, 1)),
                            y = purrr::map_dbl(d$nodes, \(v) at(v, 2))),
         edges = d$edges, exposure = d$exposure, outcome = d$outcome, latent = d$latent)
  }
}

plot_dag <- function(d) {
  parts <- .dag_parts(d)
  nodes <- parts$nodes |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      unplaced = is.na(.data$x),
      x = dplyr::if_else(.data$unplaced, 1.2 * (cumsum(.data$unplaced) - 1), .data$x),
      y = dplyr::if_else(.data$unplaced, -3, .data$y),
      half_w = 0.06 + 0.032 * nchar(.data$name),
      role = dplyr::case_when(.data$name %in% parts$exposure ~ "exposure",
                              .data$name %in% parts$outcome ~ "outcome",
                              .data$name %in% parts$latent ~ "unobserved",
                              .default = "observed"))
  # how far along a unit vector (ux, uy) the edge of a box of half-width w lies
  to_edge <- \(ux, uy, w) pmin(w / pmax(abs(ux), 1e-9), 0.15 / pmax(abs(uy), 1e-9))
  tails <- dplyr::select(nodes, from = "name", x0 = "x", y0 = "y", w0 = "half_w")
  heads <- dplyr::select(nodes, to = "name", x1 = "x", y1 = "y", w1 = "half_w")
  arrows <- parts$edges |>
    dplyr::inner_join(tails, by = "from") |>
    dplyr::inner_join(heads, by = "to") |>
    dplyr::mutate(len = sqrt((.data$x1 - .data$x0)^2 + (.data$y1 - .data$y0)^2),
                  ux = (.data$x1 - .data$x0) / .data$len,
                  uy = (.data$y1 - .data$y0) / .data$len,
                  s0 = to_edge(.data$ux, .data$uy, .data$w0),
                  s1 = to_edge(.data$ux, .data$uy, .data$w1) + 0.04,
                  x = .data$x0 + .data$s0 * .data$ux, y = .data$y0 + .data$s0 * .data$uy,
                  xend = .data$x1 - .data$s1 * .data$ux, yend = .data$y1 - .data$s1 * .data$uy)

  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(data = arrows, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
                          colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6,
                          arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(7, "pt"), type = "closed")) +
    ggplot2::geom_label(data = nodes, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, label = name, fill = role, colour = role),
                        fontface = "bold", size = 3.6, linewidth = 0,
                        label.r = grid::unit(4, "pt"), label.padding = grid::unit(5, "pt")) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(exposure = "#1b6ca8", outcome = "#d1495b",
                                          observed = "grey45", unobserved = "grey88"),
                               breaks = c("exposure", "outcome", "observed", "unobserved"),
                               name = NULL) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(exposure = "white", outcome = "white",
                                            observed = "white", unobserved = "grey25"),
                                 guide = "none") +
    # Without the override, the legend keys show the letter "a" that geom_label draws.
    ggplot2::guides(fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(override.aes = list(label = ""))) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = 0.5)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = 0.3)) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

`adjustmentSets()` returns `{ background, ideology, pessimism }`. Three paths connect concern and distrust through their common causes, and holding those three constant closes them. The two paths through the far-right vote and the verdict on services are closed already, because each runs into a common effect of concern and distrust (a collider). Holding the controls of the paper constant closes the first three paths but opens these two, and `isAdjustmentSet()` answers `FALSE`: comparing respondents who voted alike and judge the services alike makes concern and distrust go together even in this graph, in which concern has no effect on distrust at all.

Now take the `#` off the arrow `"concern -> distrust"` and run the cell again. Then try the two swaps that the cell offers, one at a time, and finally replace the arrow of the claim with `"distrust -> concern"`. Answer three questions for your own notes: whether the adjustment set changes once the arrow of the claim is on; what the far-right vote and the verdict on services become after the swaps, and what holding them constant then estimates; and whether any set of controls can separate the two directions of the arrow.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answers

1.  The set stays `{ background, ideology, pessimism }`. The arrow of the claim is the effect itself, not a path to be blocked, and the controls of the paper still open the two collider paths.
2.  After the swaps they are mediators: part of the effect of concern runs through them. Holding them constant removes that part and leaves what the graph calls the direct effect, so the controls of the paper then answer a narrower question than the claim.
3.  No. With `"distrust -> concern"`, the path `concern <- distrust` stays open whatever is held constant, and `adjustmentSets()` finds no set, so a comparison of respondents at one point in time cannot tell the two directions apart. One Multi100 analyst raised this reverse direction, and the paper says that an analysis with instrumental variables confirmed its own direction, but does not report it.

The four adjustment sets of the menu follow the graph: no controls (`"none"`), the background (`"demog"`), the background with pessimism and ideology (`"outlook"`), and those with the verdicts on the economy and public services and the two vote controls, the set of the paper (`"paper"`). The adjustment set is the second argument of `try_spec()` in Task 4, and whatever you conclude here belongs in field 4 of your preregistration in Task 5.

## Task 3 – The reproduction {#task-3-reproduction}

This is the **reproducibility** check. All five Multi100 analysts worked from one file, which a SCORE reproduction had built from the ESS files of rounds 1–4 with the variables of the paper already coded (osf.io/e48gd). Analyst 6U3LL fitted the model of Table 3 of the paper to it, without the unemployment rate of each country: a three-level model with random intercepts for countries and for country-rounds, fitted in R with the lmerTest package, which builds on lme4. Multi100 recorded **t = 46.625** on 72,733 respondents; the coefficient behind it, which the log of the analyst prints, is 0.191.

The downloadable workspace reproduces that value exactly: it downloads the file from the OSF and fits the model with lme4. This page cannot. The OSF serves the file through a redirect that does not give a page on another website permission to read it, a rule that every browser enforces (cross-origin resource sharing), and the course cannot host a copy of its own, because the file holds person-level survey data. lme4 itself runs in the browser, so the file is the only obstacle. What the page can do is fit the specification of the course that comes closest to the model of 6U3LL, on the course data: distrust of parliament, the controls of the paper, and an intercept for every country-round (fixed effects) in place of the random intercepts. The country-level variables of the paper are constant within a country-round, so the fixed effects absorb them, unemployment included.

All 192 estimates lie above zero, from 0.117 to 0.326 points of distrust per point of concern, and every one of them is significant at 5% with errors clustered by country (*t* from 11.3 to 21.6 on 15 df).
